name: stri_subset_charclass<-
title: Select Elements that Match a Given Pattern

origin.description: Replace the strings that contain a code point from a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector. The result has this length. The pattern cannot be longer than this when it is not empty.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern such as \p{L} or [a-z]. An empty pattern is an error when str is not empty.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, replace the strings that do not match. An empty string is then replaced.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Non-empty character vector written onto the matches, in order.

origin.details: A missing pattern keeps the original string. A missing string stays NA. An empty string follows negate. value is recycled over the matches only. There is no opts argument; an extra name is an unused-argument error.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as str.
origin.example:
x <- `stri_subset_charclass<-`(c("ab", "12", "c"), "\\p{L}", value = "L")
sentence <- paste0('`stri_subset_charclass<-`(c("ab", "12", "c"), "\\p{L}", value="L") returns ', paste(x, collapse = ", "), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Replace the strings that contain a code point from a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, number, logical, or list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern such as \p{L} or [a-z]. An empty pattern is an error when str is not empty.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, replace the strings that do not match. An empty string is then replaced.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings written onto the matches, in order.

translation.details: Matching is stri_subset_charclass. A missing pattern keeps the original string. A missing string stays NA. An empty string follows negate. value is recycled over the matches only. There is no opts argument; an extra name is an unused-argument error. The result is a new list.
translation.value: A list the same length as str.
translation.example:
from stringi.subset import stri_subset_charclass_assign
x = stri_subset_charclass_assign(["ab", "12", "c"], "\\p{L}", value="L")
print('`stri_subset_charclass<-`(["ab", "12", "c"], "\\p{L}", value="L") returns ' + ", ".join(x) + ".")
